title: Claude suggested a mochi jumping between blocks. I turned it into an iPhone game.
author: fuzzwaa
selftext:
The starting idea for Mori no Mochi came from Claude: a little mochi jumping between blocks. I took that suggestion and guided the game’s planning and direction, using AI tools for the code, design, and sound.



In the finished game, the blocks are tree stumps in a quiet forest. You hold your finger down to squish the mochi, then release to jump. The longer you hold, the farther it goes. Centered landings earn Perfects, and skipping a stump gives you triple points. There’s also haptic feedback as you play.



For other people making games this way: has an AI suggestion ended up becoming your main mechanic, or do you usually bring the core idea yourself?



I'm the developer. The current version is free to download and play on iPhone (iOS 17+), with ads and no in-app purchases. I plan to add in-app purchases in a future update.



[https://apps.apple.com/app/id6815947244](https://apps.apple.com/app/id6815947244)



AI also helped me draft this post.
